adjudication_records.issue_text: max_processes defaults to len(buffer.assigned_shards) when flusher_processes is None, spawning one process per shard for non-CLI construction paths (tests, direct factory wiring), causing a resource/COGS regression

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `SpanFlusher.__init__` sets `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`, so when `max_processes` is `None` it deterministically becomes `len(assigned_shards)` and results in one process/thread per shard. In `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.create_with_partitions`, `SpanFlusher(..., max_processes=self.flusher_processes, ...)` passes through `None` by default because `flusher_processes` defaults to `None` in the factory constructor. This means non-CLI construction paths that don't set `flusher_processes` will now spawn per-shard workers, which is a plausible resource/COGS regression concern. It’s not a clear correctness defect from the diff alone, but it is a concrete behavioral/operational change grounded in the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _ensure_processes_alive only checks a single per-process process_healthy_since value that main() overwrites on every successful flush of any shard, so an individual stuck shard is never detected as unhealthy

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher`, health tracking is per-process, not per-shard: `_ensure_processes_alive` only checks `self.process_healthy_since[process_index]`, and `main()` updates the passed `healthy_since.value` once per loop (before checking `if not flushed_segments:`) for the whole shard group. With shard groups (`process_to_shards_map`), there is no per-shard `healthy_since`, so a single shard making no progress could be masked as long as the process loop continues and/or other shards in that process are flushing. Whether this is a true correctness bug depends on how `SpansBuffer.flush_segments()` behaves for a “stuck shard” (not shown in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: _create_process_for_shard is dead code, never called, and the restart path in _ensure_processes_alive duplicates its shard-lookup logic inline

adjudication.rationale: In the shown diff, `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is newly added but there are no call sites to it within `flusher.py` (the restart logic in `_ensure_processes_alive` directly calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`). This makes the helper appear unused/redundant in the diff, and the restart path doesn’t leverage it, effectively duplicating the intent of “restart based on shard membership” without using the helper.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Restarts in _create_process_for_shards construct a new SpansBuffer and overwrite self.buffers[process_index] without closing the old buffer's Redis connections, leaking connections over repeated restarts

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, every restart creates a new `SpansBuffer(shards)` and then overwrites `self.buffers[process_index]` with it (`self.buffers[process_index] = shard_buffer`) without any cleanup of the previous buffer object. The diff does not show any explicit close/shutdown for `SpansBuffer`, so the specific claim about leaking Redis connections is not directly verifiable from the diff alone, but the resource-lifecycle concern created by the restart logic is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test verifies spans flow through a multi-process flusher (shard mapping bugs like dropped or double-flushed segments would go uncaught)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial shard→process mapping and multi-process management in `SpanFlusher` (`process_to_shards_map`, `num_processes`, per-process buffers, `_ensure_processes_alive`, etc.). However, the new/updated tests don’t actually exercise the multiprocessing path: when `produce_to_pipe` is provided, `SpanFlusher` uses `threading.Thread` instead of `mp_context.Process` (`if self.produce_to_pipe is None: ... Process else: ... Thread`). Both `test_basic` and the new `test_flusher_processes_limit` pass `produce_to_pipe=messages.append`, so they only validate the threaded mode and mostly assert process/shard counts, not end-to-end correctness of flushing across multiple processes (e.g., no dropped/double-flushed segments).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Restart/hang/RuntimeError path (per-process bookkeeping, MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS, process.kill) has zero test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new per-process health/restart logic in `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive()` (per-process `process_healthy_since`, `process_backpressure_since`, `process_restarts`, `process.kill()` and raising `RuntimeError` after `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`). The added/updated tests only cover normal-path behavior (`test_basic`, `test_flusher_processes_limit`) and a backpressure assertion (`any(x.value ...)`), but do not simulate a dead process (`is_alive() == False`), a hang via stale `process_healthy_since`, repeated restarts exceeding `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`, nor the `kill()`/restart path. So the finding about zero coverage for the restart/hang/RuntimeError path is supported by what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_stored_segments() and get_memory_info() are called per buffer per message, multiplying work by process count and double-counting ServiceMemory entries

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit()`, the diff changes from a single `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` call to looping over all shard-buffers: `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()` (flusher.py). That is now executed once per incoming message regardless of which shard the message pertains to, so the per-message work scales with the number of flusher buffers/processes. Similarly, the memory check now aggregates `memory_infos` by extending with `buffer.get_memory_info()` for every buffer; if `get_memory_info()` is not shard-unique (e.g., returns service-level Redis memory), this can inflate totals by counting the same `ServiceMemory` multiple times. This is a concrete performance/measurement concern grounded in the diff, though the exact double-counting behavior depends on `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` implementation not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: --flusher-processes 0 is treated as unset, silently meaning one process per shard instead of limiting

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `0` as falsy, so passing `--flusher-processes 0` (or `flusher_processes=0`) is silently ignored and becomes `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, i.e., effectively “unset / one per shard”. The click option added allows an int and does not prevent `0` (`type=int`, no range check).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code _create_process_for_shard is never called and restarts without killing the existing process first, risking process leaks

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` (flusher.py) but there are no call sites in the shown changes (restarts are done via `_ensure_processes_alive()` -> `_create_process_for_shards(...)`). As written, `_create_process_for_shard` would start a new process for the shard group via `_create_process_for_shards` without first killing/joining the existing process for that `process_index`, potentially leaving the old process running and losing its reference when `self.processes[process_index]` is overwritten. However, since it appears unused in this diff, this is primarily dead-code / future-footgun rather than a demonstrated runtime defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CLAUDE.md changes add an unrelated hasattr-vs-isinstance style rule not traced to the span-buffer PR's stated intent; should be split into a separate PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes a documentation-only change in `CLAUDE.md` adding a new style guideline about using `isinstance()` instead of `hasattr()` for union types (the added WRONG/RIGHT examples). The rest of the PR is focused on span flusher multiprocessing and related tests/options. This `CLAUDE.md` rule addition is not tied to the span flusher changes shown and constitutes scope creep that would reasonably be requested to be split into a separate PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New method `_create_process_for_shard` in flusher.py is dead code, never called in the diff, and if used would create duplicate processes racing on the same shards without killing or removing the old process

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the new helper `def _create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int):` is not referenced anywhere in the diff (all restarts go through `_ensure_processes_alive()` → `_create_process_for_shards(...)`). So the “dead code” part is verifiable. The second part is also grounded: `_create_process_for_shard` calls `_create_process_for_shards` without killing/terminating any existing process for that `process_index`, and `_create_process_for_shards` just starts a new process and overwrites `self.processes[process_index]`, which would leave the old process running if this method were ever used. Since it’s currently unused, this is not an active defect, but it is a concrete maintainability/latent-correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metric tag key inconsistency: `wait_produce` uses tag key "shards" while other flusher metrics (flusher_unhealthy, produce, segment_size_bytes) use "shard", splitting the metric series and breaking dashboards/alerts

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent metric tag keys: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use `shard`, and `_ensure_processes_alive` increments `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` with `tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard}`. However, `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`, which will split time series across different tag keys and can break existing dashboards/alerts. This is a real, diff-grounded observability issue but not a runtime correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding shard tags to existing `segment_size_bytes` and `produce` metrics causes unbounded metric cardinality over time due to rebalance-created comma-joined shard-list combinations, and is not required for health monitoring which is already covered by flusher_unhealthy/process_healthy_since

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, the diff adds `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))` and then uses it as a metric tag value for `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`. Because `shard_tag` is a comma-joined *list* of shards assigned to a process (which can change as shard→process mappings change across restarts/rebalances), this can create many distinct tag values over time (different combinations/orderings of shard sets), increasing metric cardinality. The diff already emits per-shard health metrics in `_ensure_processes_alive` via `metrics.incr(..., tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard})`, so adding shard-list tags to high-frequency metrics is a concrete observability/scope concern rather than a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _create_process_for_shard is dead code, never called, and its per-shard lookup design is vestigial and broken for the new architecture

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher` the method `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is introduced (flusher.py) but nothing in the diff calls it: initialization uses `_create_processes()`/`_create_process_for_shards`, and health checking/restarts in `_ensure_processes_alive()` also restarts via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`. As shown, `_create_process_for_shard` is therefore dead code. Since it’s unused, it doesn’t create a directly verifiable runtime defect, but it is a diff-grounded maintainability/architecture issue (leftover per-shard restart logic that no longer matches the process-per-shard-group design).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metric tag key inconsistency: 'shard' vs 'shards' across flusher metrics causes wait_produce to be silently missed by dashboards/alerts grouping by shard

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent metric tag keys in SpanFlusher: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards` instead of `shard`. This won’t break runtime behavior, but it can fragment metrics and cause dashboards/alerts grouped by `shard` to miss `wait_produce`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Class docstring claims 'one process per shard' but code creates min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards)) processes each owning a round-robin shard list

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher` the class docstring says it "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing", but the implementation computes `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` and assigns shards round-robin via `process_index = i % self.num_processes`, meaning multiple shards can share one process when `max_processes` is set (also exercised by `test_flusher_processes_limit`). This is a documentation/behavior mismatch, not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hung thread cannot be killed in thread mode; hang-restart path skips kill and starts a second concurrent flusher over the same shards causing duplicate segment production

adjudication.rationale: In thread mode (when `produce_to_pipe is not None`), `_create_process_for_shards` uses `threading.Thread` instead of a `multiprocessing.Process` (see `make_process = threading.Thread`). In `_ensure_processes_alive`, when a flusher is deemed unhealthy due to a hang (`int(time.time()) - self.process_healthy_since[...] > max_unhealthy_seconds`), the restart path only attempts `process.kill()` if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. Threads cannot be killed here, so the old hung thread is left running/alive, and the code unconditionally starts a new thread for the same `shards` via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`. That can result in multiple concurrent flushers polling/producing for the same shards, risking duplicate production if the original thread resumes or was falsely marked unhealthy.

matched_golden_ids: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe that in test_basic, time.sleep has been monkeypatched to return immediately, so calling time.sleep(0.1) does not actually wait and is effectively a no-op despite the test expecting a delay.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-buffer fan-out in submit() multiplies Redis round-trips per submitted message, creating a linear scaling cliff as flusher process count grows

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit()`, the diff changes from a single `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` call to iterating over **all** per-process buffers (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()`). It similarly aggregates memory info by calling `buffer.get_memory_info()` for every buffer. This makes the work done per submitted message scale linearly with `len(self.buffers)` / `num_processes`. If `SpansBuffer.record_stored_segments()` / `get_memory_info()` involve Redis interactions (implied by the component’s role polling Redis), this fan-out would multiply Redis round-trips as flusher process count grows, creating a scaling cliff. The scaling behavior is directly visible in the diff; the exact Redis cost is inferred from `SpansBuffer` behavior not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: max_processes falsy-value conflation: 0 silently means one process per shard instead of disabling parallelism

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` conflates `0` with `None`. If the new `--flusher-processes` option is set to `0` (allowed since `type=int` and no validation), `max_processes` becomes `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, and `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` yields one process per shard. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral bug stemming from falsy-value handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Empty assigned_shards edge case: num_processes becomes 0 so _ensure_processes_alive reports healthy forever while nothing flushes

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`. If `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty, both become 0, so `process_to_shards_map`, `processes`, `process_*` tracking dicts, and `buffers` are all empty and `_create_processes()` starts nothing. Later, `_ensure_processes_alive()` iterates over `self.processes.items()` (empty) and returns without reporting/raising, while `submit()` continues (no backpressure checks, no memory info, no flushing). This creates a silent “healthy” state where nothing flushes for the empty-shards case, which is a behavior regression versus the prior always-creating-a-process logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher.py:30 default behavior for max_processes differs between CLI (advertised default=1) and programmatic construction (one process per shard), creating inconsistent defaults and unpredictable process spawning

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two different defaults: the CLI adds a `--flusher-processes` click option with `default=1` (src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py), while programmatic construction leaves `flusher_processes` as `None` by default (factory.py), which is passed to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=None)`. In SpanFlusher, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, so `None` yields one process per shard. That creates inconsistent default behavior depending on whether the factory is built via CLI args vs directly in code, which is a concrete design/behavior inconsistency but not an immediately provable correctness defect in this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher.py:233-238 restart budget changed from flusher-wide total to per-process counter, allowing up to N × MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS crash-restart cycles before consumer restart and weakening the safety contract

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the restart budget semantics from a single flusher-wide counter (`self.process_restarts = 0` and `if self.process_restarts > MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS: raise ...`) to a per-process counter (`self.process_restarts = {process_index: 0 ...}` and `if self.process_restarts[process_index] > MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS: raise ...; self.process_restarts[process_index] += 1`). This means with `num_processes > 1`, the consumer could tolerate up to `num_processes * MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` total crashes before restarting the consumer, which is a real change in the safety/operational contract. It’s not provably incorrect from the diff alone (could be intended for isolation), but it is a concrete, diff-grounded behavioral weakening worth calling out.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher.py:31 class docstring claims one process per shard but implementation uses round-robin shard sharing when max_processes < len(shards), misleading readers about per-shard health isolation

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher` docstring the diff now states: "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing." However the implementation explicitly allows shard sharing when `max_processes` is set: `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` and shards are assigned round-robin via `process_index = i % self.num_processes`, meaning a single process can handle multiple shards. Health/backpressure tracking is also per-process (`process_healthy_since`, `process_backpressure_since`) and uses a combined `shard_tag` (comma-joined list), so it is not strictly per-shard isolated. This is a documentation/expectations mismatch, not a demonstrated functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher.py:116 _create_process_for_shard is dead code duplicating the restart path and misleadingly suggesting per-shard restart granularity exists

adjudication.rationale: In flusher.py a helper `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is introduced, but the diff shows no call sites for it. The actual restart logic in `_ensure_processes_alive` restarts via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` directly, not per-shard. As written, `_create_process_for_shard` is unused/dead code and suggests a finer-grained restart capability than exists (it still restarts the whole process for that shard-group). This is a maintainability/clarity issue rather than a demonstrated runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher.py:198-203 metric tag keys are inconsistent within the same loop (shard vs shards, per-shard integer), fragmenting previously untagged series and breaking dashboards/alerts without migration or deprecation

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent metrics tag keys/values introduced in flusher.py: in `main()`, `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing(..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use key `shard`, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. Also `_ensure_processes_alive()` now emits `metrics.incr(..., tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard})` where `shard` is an int, whereas other places use the comma-joined string `shard_tag`. This will split/fragment metric series (and changes previously untagged `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` into per-shard series) which can break dashboards/alerts unless handled intentionally. It’s an observability/compatibility concern rather than a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher.py:301-303 health/drift computation now depends on freshly constructed SpansBuffer objects separate from the writer's buffer, breaking the invariant that flusher health view matches actual stored state

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show SpanFlusher now constructs new `SpansBuffer` instances per process (`shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)` in `_create_process_for_shards`) and no longer stores/uses the original `buffer` passed to `__init__` except for `buffer.assigned_shards`. That is a concrete architectural/state-consistency concern: the flusher’s health/backpressure/memory checks and flushing logic operate on these new buffer instances (`self.buffers[...]`, `buffer.record_stored_segments()`, `buffer.get_memory_info()`), which may diverge from any state held by the writer’s original buffer if `SpansBuffer` has in-memory state beyond shard assignment. However, the finding’s claim about “drift computation” depending on the new buffers is not supported by the diff (drift is via `current_drift.value`), and whether this truly “breaks the invariant” can’t be verified from the diff alone without `SpansBuffer` internals.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CLAUDE.md:448-456 unrelated hasattr/isinstance doc change is scope accretion riding on a PR about span-buffer multiprocess work

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new documentation snippet in CLAUDE.md about avoiding `hasattr()` for unions and using `isinstance()` instead (lines around 445+), which is unrelated to the substantive code changes in this PR (adding flusher process parallelism, new CLI option `--flusher-processes`, and associated tests). This is verifiable scope accretion: a standalone doc change “riding along” with the span-buffer multiprocess work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _create_process_for_shard is dead code

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the method `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is defined but, within the diff, nothing calls it (the class uses `_create_processes()`, `_create_process_for_shards()`, and `_ensure_processes_alive()` instead). As a private helper, this strongly suggests it is currently unused/dead code (though it could be referenced elsewhere outside the shown diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Killed processes are never removed from self.processes/self.buffers before being replaced

adjudication.rationale: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, when a process is deemed unhealthy it calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, which assigns `self.processes[process_index] = process` and `self.buffers[process_index] = shard_buffer`, overwriting the existing entries for that `process_index` (i.e., effectively replacing/removing the old references). The diff does not show a case where killed processes/buffers accumulate in these dicts due to not being removed first; they are replaced in-place.

adjudication_records.issue_text: threading.Thread has no kill() path for terminating processes

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, unhealthy workers are restarted, but termination is only attempted when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` (i.e., `process.kill()`), and threads get no termination path. When `produce_to_pipe` is set, workers are created as `threading.Thread` (`make_process = threading.Thread`), so a hung thread (`cause = "hang"` based on `process_healthy_since`) will not be stopped before `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement thread. This can leak the original thread and potentially duplicate flushing work since the shared `stopped` flag is only set during `join()`, not during restarts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts internal data structures (process count, max_processes, total_shards) with no behavioral coverage: no messages submitted, no commits or produced payloads checked, so the new multiprocess shard-sharing flush behavior is never exercised

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the test only inspects internal fields created during `create_with_partitions` (`len(flusher.processes)`, `flusher.max_processes`, `flusher.num_processes`, and `process_to_shards_map` totals) and then calls `step.join()` without ever submitting messages, polling, or asserting on produced payloads/commits. As a result, the new shard-to-process sharing and flushing behavior added in `SpanFlusher.main`/`submit`/`_ensure_processes_alive` is not actually exercised; it’s configuration/structure coverage rather than behavioral coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: total_shards == 4 assertion is tautological since the map is built by iterating buffer.assigned_shards, so the sum always equals the shard count by construction

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit`, `total_shards` is compared to a constant (`4`) derived from the test setup (`partitions = {... for i in range(4)}`). While `process_to_shards_map` is indeed constructed by iterating `buffer.assigned_shards` (so `sum(len(...)) == len(buffer.assigned_shards)` by construction), the assertion is not tautological with respect to the test’s expectation: it can still fail if `buffer.assigned_shards` is not correctly derived from the 4 input partitions. So the finding overstates the issue as “always equals 4.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: The rewritten health/restart machinery in _ensure_processes_alive is entirely untested: dead-process detection, hang detection via process_healthy_since, MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError, thread-mode kill guard, and the restart call are never triggered by any test

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new health/restart logic in `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive()` (per-process `process_healthy_since`, `process_backpressure_since`, `process_restarts`, `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` RuntimeError path, and restart via `_create_process_for_shards`). The added/updated tests (`test_basic`, `test_flusher_processes_limit`, and the backpressure assertion change) only verify process-count/shard distribution and that backpressure flags can be set, but they never force a flusher worker to die (`is_alive() == False`), never advance time to trigger the hang condition (`time.time() - process_healthy_since[...] > max_unhealthy_seconds`), never drive the repeated-restart counter to hit `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`, and never exercise the kill/restart behavior (notably tests run in thread-mode via `produce_to_pipe=messages.append`, so the `multiprocessing.Process.kill()` branch is also unexercised). This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test gap for new nontrivial behavior, not a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The added time.sleep(0.1) for drift propagation in test_consumer.py is a no-op because monkeypatch.setattr('time.sleep', lambda _: None) replaces the sleep attribute on the time module itself, so the race it claims to fix is not mitigated

adjudication.rationale: In `test_basic` the test does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, which replaces `time.sleep` on the `time` module. The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` later in the same test therefore becomes a no-op, so it cannot “give flusher threads time to process” as the comment claims. This makes the intended race mitigation ineffective in the test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The per-process join loop in flusher.py join() applies the deadline sequentially, so a hung first process consumes the entire timeout leaving zero drain time for remaining processes

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), a single global `deadline` is computed and then applied while iterating processes sequentially. If the first process remains alive until `deadline` passes, the loop will exit early via `if remaining_time <= 0: break`, meaning later processes are neither waited on nor terminated (since termination happens after the per-process wait). This matches the finding: a hung first process can consume the whole timeout and leave no time/cleanup for remaining processes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remaining_time is computed and compared but never otherwise used in join(), indicating an intended per-process timeout split that was never implemented

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), remaining_time is computed and then immediately used in a comparison (`if remaining_time <= 0: break`). The actual timeout behavior is enforced via the shared `deadline` check in the inner `while process.is_alive() and (deadline is None or deadline > time.time())` loop. The diff does not show any broken behavior or a clearly intended but missing “per-process timeout split”; at most it’s a small redundancy/cleanup nit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test exercises join with multiple processes and a timeout, leaving the starvation behavior unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new multi-process shutdown logic in `SpanFlusher.join(self, timeout=...)`, including a deadline-based loop over `self.processes` and timeout handling (`deadline`, `remaining_time`, breaking when exceeded). Existing/new tests (`test_basic`, `test_flusher_processes_limit`) call `step.join()` with no timeout and do not cover the new join-with-timeout behavior when multiple processes exist, so the starvation/timeout path is unverified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The assert any() over process_backpressure_since.values() masks a process whose backpressure tracking is broken, since a regressed process hides behind a healthy sibling in multi-process setups

adjudication.rationale: In tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py the assertion was changed from checking a single backpressure_since value to `assert any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values())`. Given the new multi-process design in SpanFlusher (per-process `process_backpressure_since` dict), this test now only verifies that at least one process reported backpressure, and would still pass if another process’s backpressure tracking were broken or never set. This is a test/verification gap introduced by the diff rather than a directly provable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Partition-rebalance changes are invisible to the shard→process map: process_to_shards_map and per-process SpansBuffer shards are computed once in __init__ from buffer.assigned_shards, so newly assigned shards after rebalance are never polled and their Redis-buffered spans are stranded, causing silent data loss if the strategy is reused across rebalances

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `SpanFlusher.__init__` derives `self.process_to_shards_map` once from `buffer.assigned_shards` and then creates per-process `SpansBuffer(shards)` instances stored in `self.buffers`. There is no mechanism shown to update that mapping or recreate per-process buffers if the set of assigned shards changes later. However, the finding’s claim of “silent data loss if the strategy is reused across rebalances” depends on lifecycle/rebalance behavior not shown in the diff (e.g., whether `SpanFlusher` is recreated on rebalance), so it’s a concrete edge-case/architecture concern but not verifiable as an actual bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _create_process_for_shard (singular) is dead code with no call site; every restart path uses _create_process_for_shards, and its misleading name suggests per-shard restart granularity exists

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the method `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is added, but within the shown diff there is no call site for it. Process creation/restart flows use `_create_processes()` -> `_create_process_for_shards(...)` and `_ensure_processes_alive()` restarts via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`. This makes `_create_process_for_shard` effectively dead code in this change and its name implies per-shard restart granularity that is not actually used (restarts are per process/shard-group). This is a maintainability/clarity issue rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'if not process: continue' guard in _ensure_processes_alive is dead since process values are always truthy SpawnProcess/Thread objects, masking the fact that dead processes are tracked solely by process_restarts which never decrements or removes entries

adjudication.rationale: The guard `if not process: continue` in `_ensure_processes_alive` is indeed redundant because `process` entries are created as `SpawnProcess` or `threading.Thread` objects (`_create_process_for_shards`) and the loop iterates over existing dict values, so they will be truthy. However, the finding’s claim that this “masks” dead-process tracking is not supported by the diff: dead/hung processes are detected via `process.is_alive()` and `process_healthy_since[...]` and are actively restarted by overwriting `self.processes[process_index]`. `process_restarts` is a monotonic counter by design, not something that should “decrement or remove entries.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: Threaded-mode hang restart spawns a new thread without terminating the hung old thread, causing unbounded thread growth and concurrent flushers racing on the same Redis shards

adjudication.rationale: In threaded mode (`produce_to_pipe` not None), `_create_process_for_shards` uses `threading.Thread` and stores it in `self.processes`. When `_ensure_processes_alive` detects an unhealthy flusher, it only attempts to `kill()` if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`; for threads it does nothing (catches `AttributeError`) and then immediately calls `_create_process_for_shards(...)`, starting a new thread while the old hung thread is still alive. Since the shard assignment (`process_to_shards_map`) is unchanged, both threads can operate on the same Redis shards, and repeated restarts can lead to unbounded thread growth and racing flushers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Negative --flusher-processes value crashes consumer startup with a cryptic KeyError: 0 due to no lower-bound validation on the CLI option

adjudication.rationale: The new CLI option `--flusher-processes` is declared as `type=int` with no lower-bound validation, so negative values are accepted. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `-1` as truthy, so `self.max_processes` becomes `-1`. Then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` yields `-1`, causing `process_to_shards_map = {i: [] for i in range(self.num_processes)}` to be empty (`range(-1)`), and the subsequent loop does `process_index = i % self.num_processes` (0 for `% -1`) and attempts `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)`, raising `KeyError: 0`. This would crash consumer startup with a cryptic KeyError as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: _create_process_for_shard is never called and would bypass the kill/restart-count bookkeeping and MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS guard if used

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher` (`src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`), `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is added but is not referenced anywhere in the shown diff (no call sites). That makes it dead/unreachable code as-is. Also, unlike `_ensure_processes_alive()`, it restarts a process via `_create_process_for_shards(...)` without incrementing `self.process_restarts[...]`, checking `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`, or attempting to kill/terminate the existing process, so if it were later used it could bypass the intended restart/guard bookkeeping.

adjudication_records.issue_text: When join deadline expires, processes not yet iterated never get terminate() called and stay alive past the timeout with no log

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), the loop over self.processes breaks when the deadline is exceeded (`if remaining_time <= 0: break`). Because `process.terminate()` is only called inside that per-process loop, any processes not yet iterated will not have `terminate()` invoked and can remain alive past the timeout. The diff also shows no logging/reporting on this path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metric tag-key typo: produce timer uses tags={"shard": ...} while wait timer uses tags={"shards": ...}, splitting the metric series and breaking per-shard observability

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the produce timer uses `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, but the wait timer uses `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})`. This tag-key mismatch is verifiable in the diff and would split metric series / prevent consistent per-shard breakdown, but it doesn’t change core runtime correctness (it’s an observability issue).
